**CHA2DS2-VASc** is a clinical risk scoring system utilized to assess the thromboembolic risk—specifically the risk of [[iskaemisk-apopleksi|ischemic stroke]]—in patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]]. Within the framework of the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database]], it functions as the primary decision-support tool for determining the indication for [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]] [^src11], [^src17]. The score is a cornerstone of the [[abc-pathway|ABC Pathway]] model for stroke avoidance and is heavily integrated into national clinical quality indicators [^src8].

In the specific methodology applied by the Danish registry, a score of ≥2 is the universal threshold for indicating anticoagulation therapy for both men and women. This is because the calculation rules used in these reports do not assign points for female sex, making ≥2 the definitive cutoff for treatment eligibility across both sexes [^src1], [^src7], [^src12], [^src17]. The score defines the target population (the denominator) for key quality metrics, such as [[indikator-1|Indicator 1]], which measures the [[ventetid-til-antikoagulations-behandling|waiting time for anticoagulation treatment]] [^src9], [^src17], and [[indikator-4a|Indicator 4a]], which tracks treatment coverage over time [^src12].

Data from the reporting period of July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, highlights the score's distribution and clinical impact across Denmark. The average CHA2DS2-VASc score for incident (newly diagnosed) atrial fibrillation patients was reported as 1.73 [^src1] and 1.75 [^src6], while the average for prevalent patients was 1.47 [^src1]. Approximately 60.21% of incident patients had a score of ≥2, thus meeting the criteria for anticoagulation [^src6]. Demonstrating high clinical performance, national metrics showed that 92% of newly diagnosed patients with a score ≥2 were successfully initiated on oral anticoagulation within 30 days of their diagnosis [^src11], [^src17].

Beyond treatment indication, the score is critical for safety and risk-stratification analyses, particularly concerning bleeding complications. Supplementary analyses for [[indikator-6|Indicator 6]] and [[indikator-7|Indicator 7]] reveal a paradoxical distribution of bleeding events among lower-risk cohorts. Specifically, 41.1% of [[intrakraniel-bloedning|intracranial bleedings]] occurred in patients with a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 0 or 1 [^src3]. Similarly, 43.7% of [[alvorlig-bloedning|major bleedings]] were observed in patients with a score of 0 or 1 [^src4], [^src13], [^src14]. Among prevalent patients who suffered an intracranial bleed, 36.7% had a score of exactly 1 [^src15]. These findings underscore the ongoing clinical challenge of balancing thromboembolic prevention with bleeding risks in everyday practice.
